<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s).

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 944f03850ec68ffb52374ce51424074f9e43b564`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `enforceAuth (23 routes)`, `resolveExecCtx (28 routes)`, `routeManager (20 routes)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 944f03850ec68ffb52374ce51424074f9e43b564` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `abd4663d03b59e1da60c04d08d5062fac18b43f7` — the merge of head `35f207b70e9155039b2f71a65cbd9e9c682a7ad9` into base `944f03850ec68ffb52374ce51424074f9e43b564`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin abd4663d03b59e1da60c04d08d5062fac18b43f7 && git checkout abd4663d03b59e1da60c04d08d5062fac18b43f7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 944f03850ec68ffb52374ce51424074f9e43b564 35f207b70e9155039b2f71a65cbd9e9c682a7ad9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 944f03850ec68ffb52374ce51424074f9e43b564 && git merge --no-ff 35f207b70e9155039b2f71a65cbd9e9c682a7ad9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 944f03850ec68ffb52374ce51424074f9e43b564
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 944f03850ec68ffb52374ce51424074f9e43b564` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `35f207b70e9155039b2f71a65cbd9e9c682a7ad9`
Local-runs: none

**Face:** the declaration face. This is a move-only slice of `@objectstack/rest`, and no token of the moved body changed. The diff does six things:
- it moves one registrar body into one new module, `packages/rest/src/email-routes.ts`;
- it adds `export` to one module-level helper, `seamOrUndefined`;
- it grows the registrar list 8 → 9 and re-points the nine readers of that list;
- it re-points one more test reader, `objectql-slot-consumer-census.test.ts`;
- it re-points one gate's target table, `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`;
- it re-points one platform-checklist item (two strings).

The 15-file list holds no published schema and no governed path. `record-recognisers --template --paths` over that list derives `TIER_DEFAULT`. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded success. The PR body reads `Clause-②: no` with no arm, and the diff adds no changeset.

**Inputs:**
- card #23050: its body and all 34 comments. These include the triage `6126748916`, slice 1's landing `6136102437`, slice 2's refinement `6189011700`, the seat ruling `6205442867`, slice 7's release `6206265218`, the slice 8 claim `6213111311` and the slice 8 report `6214413749`;
- slice 7's record `6205886625` on PR #23763, used as precedent;
- PR #23882:
  - its body;
  - its file list: 15 files, +299 / −127, which matches `git diff --numstat` file for file;
  - its one comment, the advisory Docs Drift Check;
  - its timeline: the labels, and the declarations `6214477252` on #6017 and `6214486315` on #6023;
- the net diff against the merge base `6422da58e8`;
- the 44 check-runs on this head, read last.

**Method:** read-only. Every count below was read off the git objects of the merge base and the head with `git show`, text `diff` and `grep`. Each reader's own rule was applied to that text: the execctx site rule, the docblock opener rule, `scanSource`'s two dialect rules and the two realtime tripwire regexes. Nothing was built, tested or re-run. The merge base's `rest-server.ts` blob (`730c2aaa03`) is the same blob as at the dev's base `f7e836da1e`, so the PR's base line numbers apply as written. Between `f7e836da1e` and the merge base, nothing changed under `packages/rest`, `packages/qa` or `docs/qa`, or in the gate.

### ① Derived judgments

No accept set changes and no public surface changes. Each change the diff makes is judged below.

1. **The moved body is byte-identical once de-indented: right.**
   - Base `rest-server.ts` `:9083`–`:9176` is 94 lines. With one 4-space indent removed, it equals head `email-routes.ts` `:70`–`:163`, and `diff` finds 0 differing lines.
   - The range holds 3 empty lines. It has no whitespace-only line and no trailing whitespace.
   - Its one template literal, `${basePath}/email/send` (base `:9086`), sits on one line. Every other line with a backtick is a line comment. So removing the indent changed no runtime string.
   - The body has no `RestServer.` access. The claim's `static` exception was not used, and no token changed.
   - The rest of `rest-server.ts` changes in three hunks, +15 / −95 in total:
     - the import and its comment (head `:342`–`:343`);
     - `export` on `seamOrUndefined` (head `:1495`);
     - the stub, 12 lines in place of the 94.
   - The file goes from 10,127 to 10,047 lines.
   - The private method keeps its name, its JSDoc (head `:9064`–`:9083`) and its position.
   - The call site in `registerForBase` is unchanged: base `:4806`, head `:4808`.
     - It is still unconditional for each base.
     - It still sits between `registerSearchEndpoints` and `registerFormEndpoints`.
     - So the registration order holds on every base.

2. **The host lists exactly what the body reads: right.**
   - The body's code reads of `this.` (comments excluded):
     - `emailServiceProvider` 2 (module `:80` and `:109`);
     - `routeManager` 1 (`:71`);
     - `resolveExecCtx` 1 (`:77`);
     - `enforceAuth` 1 (`:78`).
   - A third mention of `this.emailServiceProvider` (`:105`) sits inside a comment.
   - `EmailRouteHost` (`:56`–`:61`) declares exactly these 4. Each is typed by indexed access on the class.
   - The body has no bare `this`, no element access on `this` and no `function` keyword.
   - It reads two module-level bindings:
     - `logError`, imported from `./log.js` as `rest-server.ts` imports it (6 calls stay there);
     - `seamOrUndefined`.
   - `String` is a global.
   - So the dev's finding is right: the claim's hypothesis (1) was partly wrong.
     - `tenancyServiceProvider`, `kernelManager` and `resolveRequestEnvironmentId` are read by the next method, `resolveAnonymousFormTenancy` (base `:9185`).
     - That method did not move.

3. **Value or getter, field by field: right.**
   - **`routeManager` goes by value.**
     - Its one read is the top-level `register` call, which runs during registration.
     - The class reassigns the field only at head `:5177` / `:5181`, in the try/finally around `registerMetadataEndpointsInner`.
     - `registerForBase` calls the email registrar outside that window.
   - **`emailServiceProvider` goes as a getter.**
     - Both code reads are inside the handler, so they run at request time.
     - The field (head `:2093`) is `private` and not `readonly`. Only the constructor assigns it (head `:2175`).
     - A copy taken at registration would not follow a later assignment.
     - The getter reads through a closure on the server (`readEmailServiceProvider`), in slice 5's spelling. This is slice 2's refinement, applied to this one field.
   - **The two methods go as late-bound closures.** So their receiver is still the server, and a spy set after registration is still the one reached.
   - The dev's getter measurement (501 then 200) and by-value ablation (frozen at 501) are the dev's, not re-run here. They match this reading.

4. **`seamOrUndefined` gains `export`, and it does not reach the published `.d.ts`: right.**
   - There is one declaration (head `:1495`), and the module imports it. Nothing is copied.
   - 5 code uses stay in `rest-server.ts`: head `:3121`, `:3129`, `:3144`, `:3192` and `:3352`.
   - **Why the `.d.ts` does not change:**
     - `@objectstack/rest` publishes `dist` only.
     - The root `tsup.config.ts` builds it from the single entry `src/index.ts`, with `splitting: false`, and emits the `.d.ts` from that entry.
     - `src/index.ts` is untouched. It re-exports from `./rest-server.js` by name only: `RestServer`, the types `RestProtocol` and `MountedRoute`, and `metaItemPackageBinding`.
     - It has no `export *`. It names neither `seamOrUndefined` nor the new module.
     - `EmailRouteHost` appears only inside a private method body, which declaration emit does not reach.
   - This is the same class of edit as slice 5's `export function mayReadPendingDrafts`.
   - The new import cycle is harmless.
     - `seamOrUndefined` is a hoisted function declaration, read only at request time.
     - Earlier modules already import values from `rest-server.ts`, for example `discovery-routes.ts` and `batch-routes.ts`.
   - The dev's `.d.ts` sha and export-list readings are the dev's, not re-run here. They are what this construction predicts.

5. **The registrar list and every reader were re-counted, and no reader was loosened: right.**
   - The list grows 8 → 9 by one appended entry. All nine importers of the list are in the diff, and each moves its length pin 8 → 9.
   - **execctx census.** Its site rule counts lines that hold `this.resolveExecCtx(environmentId, req)`.
     - Sites: 62 at both. Base 25 + 9 + 5 + 7 + 8 + 1 + 5 + 2; head 24 + 9 + 5 + 7 + 8 + 1 + 5 + 2 + 1.
     - Split: 46 bare / 16 caught at both. Each of the 46 bare sites is followed by the `enforceAuth` guard line, the email site included (`:78`).
     - Mentions of `resolveExecCtx`: 113 → 117. `rest-server.ts` goes 57 → 58 (one site out, one forwarder's 2 mentions in). The module holds 3 (the site 1, the interface member 2).
     - Forwarder lines in `rest-server.ts`: 9 → 10. The pin is exact: (9 − 1) + 3 − 1 = 10.
     - Neither map gains an entry. That is right, because the module carries one registrar and that registrar reads the seam.
   - **ui-view pair** (counted over the list):
     - `this.enforceAuth(` 56 → 57 and `this.resolveExecCtx(` 71 → 72.
     - `rest-server.ts` stays at 19 and 34 (one site out, one forwarder in).
     - The floors of 40 are unchanged.
   - **dogfood blind-spot row:**
     - `this.routeManager.register(` stays at 63 = 22 + 9 + 5 + 7 + 8 + 1 + 6 + 4 + 1.
     - `private register*Endpoints(` 16, `registerPerItemRoute(` 8 and `const registerPerItemRoute =` 1 are each unchanged.
     - The population 70 / 19 / 51 is unchanged: 63 − 1 + 8 = 70. The email door is outside `registerMetadataEndpoints` before and after.
     - **`enforceAuth` goes 96 → 100**: `rest-server.ts` 41 → 42, and the module 3.
       - The four new mentions are the seam once: the forwarder 2, the interface member 2.
       - No call site was added.
       - It is an exact re-anchor, as in slices 3–7.
     - The new control `email-routes.ts: this.routeManager.register(` reads 1. `registrar list length` reads 9.
   - **docblock pin:**
     - The module has exactly 3 TSDoc openers (`:3`, `:49`, `:63`), and its floor is 3.
     - The moved range held 0, so `rest-server.ts` keeps 164 at base and head (floor 100).
     - The floors' sum goes 34 → 37, and the sum is pinned exactly.
   - **query-number 9, canonical-query 4, meta-draft 8:**
     - The module has 0 `Number` / `parseInt` / `parseFloat` tokens, 0 `query:` text and 0 draft tokens.
     - Each new floor is 0, and each sum is unchanged.
   - **dogfood realtime tripwire:** both probe regexes read 0 on each of the nine files.

6. **`objectql-slot-consumer-census.test.ts` is re-pointed, not loosened: right.**
   - Its §1 controls read `emailServiceProvider` twice: as the known-present sibling slot, and as the window predicate's negative. Those reads moved.
   - At head, `rest-server.ts` still holds one read of the field (the stub's closure) but no call of it. So `wrappedIn('emailServiceProvider', 'seamOrUndefined(')` would read 0 there. Re-pointing both controls to the module is the honest move.
   - Read on `email-routes.ts`:
     - 2 read sites (`:80`, `:109`) and 1 call site (`:109`);
     - `seamOrUndefined(` 1 and `wiredEngineOrLoud(` 0 in the call's window.
   - The expected values (more than 0, then 1, then 0) did not change.
   - The `objectQLProvider` census (3 sites over `SLOT_FILES`) is untouched, and so is `SLOT_FILES`. The module holds no `objectQLProvider` site.
   - The removed local `lines` had one user, and that user now reads `emailLines`.

7. **`scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` is re-pointed, not loosened: right.**
   - Counted on the module by `scanSource`'s own rules:
     - `stringError` is 1: `:120`, `error: 'JSON body required'`.
     - `siblingCode` is 3: `:120`, `:143` and `:153` (`INVALID_REQUEST`, `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `EMAIL_SEND_FAILED`).
     - The two 501 bodies (`:81`, `:111`) carry `code` and `message` but no `error`, so neither rule counts them.
     - `:134` and `:137` pass a variable, not a literal.
   - The body moved byte for byte, and the stub has no `.json(` call. So `rest-server.ts` drops by exactly those counts: 17 → 16 and 17 → 14.
   - Both sums hold:
     - `stringError`: 16 + 13 + 8 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 1 = 39;
     - `siblingCode`: 14 + 15 + 8 + 9 + 4 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 3 = 54.
   - `auditDialectOnly` requires each count to equal its pin and reds in both directions. So the pins are as tight as before.
   - The new entry is `dialectOnly` with ratchet `#9559`, like the seven moved modules before it.
   - A `MODULES` declaration also takes the file out of the express-writer walk (`discoverExpressRoutes`). So no `EXPRESS_RESPONSE_MODULES` entry is owed.
   - Both new history comments say "NOT progress — the same MOVE".
   - Slice 6's "two arms" carry was already closed by slice 7 ("four arms"). This slice appends after it.
   - `Lint · docs & code guards` concluded success.

8. **The checklist JSON re-point is pure: right.**
   - In `integration-system.json`, two strings change:
     - the source entry `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts#registerEmailEndpoints (…)` becomes `packages/rest/src/email-routes.ts#registerEmailEndpoints (…)`;
     - the `verify` prose's file name changes the same way.
   - All other text is unchanged.
   - The new anchor names an exported function at that path (`:69`).
   - The answers the entry lists are the moved body's: 401, 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, `VALIDATION_FAILED`, 501, and 500 `EMAIL_SEND_FAILED`.
   - `check:platform-checklist` is kept out of per-PR CI by design. The dev's local reading (735 / 745 anchors resolved before and after; cited sources 347 → 348) is the dev's.

9. **The readers left untouched read no moved line: right.**
   - **Line citations:** none of the tree's `rest-server.ts:NNNN` citations falls in the moved range `:9063`–`:9177`. Outside released CHANGELOG text, the highest is `:5872`.
   - **ADR anchors:** the moved body cites no `ADR-NNNN Dk`, so no ADR anchor is owed. The `rest-server.ts` ADR anchor names no email symbol.
   - **`packages/spec`:**
     - No `packages/spec/liveness` row cites the email registrar, the route or a moved line.
     - `discovery.zod.ts` `:396` names the method, and the method still registers the door.
   - **Other source readers of `rest-server.ts` read regions this move does not touch:**
     - `execctx-authz-input-seam-reachability` reads `computeExecCtx` only, and its `seamOrUndefined(` sites are there;
     - `auth-gate-allowlist-fault-window` reads the auth gate;
     - `meta-list-projection-parity` reads the `/meta` routes;
     - `authz-store-unavailable` checks for other tokens' presence;
     - `check-system-context-census` anchors the `enforceAuth` declaration;
     - `check-single-authz-resolver` lists the file as a delegator.
   - **Gates that walk `packages/rest/src` still reach the moved code in its new file.** These are `check-rest-log-declared`, `check-durability-degradation-log-level`, `check-meta-type-normalized`, `check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary` and `check-error-status-conformance`. The moved `logError` call is among what they reach.
   - **Prose that names the method or the door without a file stays true.** This covers `getMountedEmailRouteBase`'s docblock (head `:9991`), `discovery-routes.ts` `:304` and the two parity tests.

### ② Semver level

- **`skip-changeset` is right.** Nothing a released package publishes changes.
  - **`@objectstack/rest`:**
    - The `.d.ts` and the export list hold by construction (① item 4).
    - The routes and their registration order hold by the move (① item 1).
  - **The rest of the diff:**
    - tests, including `@objectstack/dogfood`'s;
    - comments;
    - one gate's target table;
    - the checklist JSON.
  - **The one runtime difference is the provider's call receiver (③ item 1).**
    - The provider's declared type has no `this`.
    - No shipped wiring can observe it.
    - So it is not a published behaviour.
  - A move that changes no behaviour is not a feature or a fix. So no `patch` changeset is owed, the same reading slices 1–7 landed on.
- **`Clause-②: no` is right.**
  - The door reads `req.params.environmentId` and `req.body`, as before.
  - No route is added or removed, and no `spec` key moves.
  - No accept set widens or narrows, so no `(narrowing)` arm is owed.
  - Line 2 of the PR body carries the line. No changeset exists to carry it a second time.
- **The changeset check's history:**
  - `Check Changeset` concluded failure at 11:22:37Z, before the label.
  - `skip-changeset` was written at 11:25:59Z by `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, the seat's write path.
  - The re-run concluded `skipped` at 11:26:01Z.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag is answered or escalated. The flags come from two places: the PR body's Acceptance notes, and the report's (`6214413749`) `deviations` and `out_of_scope_findings`. The report's `open_questions` is empty.

1. **Acceptance note and out-of-scope finding 1: the provider's call receiver. ESCALATED to the seat, non-blocking.**
   - The finding is right.
     - Through the host, `this.emailServiceProvider!(environmentId)` (`:109`) calls the provider with the host literal as receiver.
     - At base, the receiver was the server.
   - Only a non-arrow provider that reads `this` could observe the change.
     - The constructor parameter's type declares no `this`.
     - The shipped provider (`rest-api-plugin.ts` `:406`) is an `async` arrow.
   - It is not new to this slice. `main` already calls six providers through host getters, at these sites:
     - `batch-routes.ts` `:172` and `approvals-routes.ts` `:97`;
     - `sharing-routes.ts` `:108` and `:563`;
     - `analytics-routes.ts` `:105`;
     - `security-routes.ts` `:124` and `:417`.
     - No earlier record named the property.
   - Leaving it as it is is right for this slice. A bound hand-over would be a new host shape, which the claim forbids.
   - **For the seat:** should later slices hand providers over bound? That includes the CRUD and `/meta` slices. It is a pattern question and the seat's ruling, like `6205442867`.
2. **Acceptance note: the moved `[#15405]` comment still reads true.** Verified.
   - The `if (!this.emailServiceProvider)` guard is above it, at `:80`.
   - The shipped provider is `async` (`rest-api-plugin.ts` `:406`).
3. **Deviation: hypothesis (1) partly falsified.** Answered: verified (① item 2). Nothing past base `:9177` moved.
4. **Deviation: the `static` exception unused.** Answered: verified (① item 1). No token changed.
5. **Deviation: `export` on `seamOrUndefined`.** Answered: right (① item 4).
6. **Deviation: readers edited beyond the claim's named families.**
   - These are the objectql census and the checklist `verify` prose.
   - Answered: each reads a moved line, and each edit is a pure re-point (① items 6 and 8).
   - Both cross-lane edits were declared before this review:
     - the checklist edit on #6023 (`6214486315`);
     - the gate edit on #6017 (`6214477252`).
7. **Deviation: `getMountedEmailRouteBase`'s docblock was not edited.** Answered: right.
   - It sits on a class member that ships in the `.d.ts`.
   - It names the method, and the method still registers the route.
   - Slices 6 and 7 handled such docblocks the same way.
8. **Deviation: one merge of `origin/main` (`6422da58e8`).** Answered: it is disjoint.
   - The merge commit changes none of the 15 files.
   - `main` is now 11 commits further on, at `94114c1f2`. None of them touches `packages/rest`, the gate, `docs/qa` or the re-pointed dogfood files.
9. **The other deviations are not contract matters:**
   - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exiting 3, then 0;
   - the lock's batch-last-exit line;
   - the commit trailers;
   - the scratch and worktree notes.
10. **Deviation: the red-before of `authz-conformance.test.ts` was not observed.** Answered: not blocking.
    - The file pins the list's length plus a zero over the list.
    - The static recount (① item 5) reads 0 on all nine files.
11. **Out-of-scope finding 2: `packages/spec/src/api/discovery.zod.ts` `:396`.** Answered.
    - It names the method, not a file, and it stays true.
    - No carry is owed. No `packages/spec` file is edited, as the claim ordered.
12. **Out-of-scope finding 3: `meta-state-route-engine-outage.test.ts` `:95`.** Note only, 承接者:无.
    - Its "in this file" is dated history about `rest-server.ts`.
    - The test reads no source.
13. **Out-of-scope finding 4: stale `rest-server.ts` line citations.** Answered.
    - None falls in the moved range (① item 9).
    - Every line after `:342` moved down by 2, as each earlier slice's import moved them.
14. **New from this review: one new header sentence is wrong for one mode. Non-blocking.**
    - The new module header (`email-routes.ts` `:7`–`:8`) says "an environment-scoped deployment mounts the door twice".
    - That holds only for `projectResolution` `optional` or `auto`.
    - Under `required`, `registerRoutes` mounts the scoped base alone, so the door mounts once (head `:4851`–`:4853`). The dev's own `scoped-required` dump counts 1 door.
    - It is new prose, not moved text, and no behaviour depends on it. The seat may have it fixed in one line before landing, or carry it to the module's next edit.
15. **The dogfood pair has no PR-time verdict.**
    - The sharded `Dogfood Regression Gate` leg and `Dogfood Verify CLI` skipped. The aggregate `Dogfood Regression Gate` concluded success.
